results.title: Fix Teams Meeting add-in problems in Classic Outlook - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
results.content:
Important

The new Outlook for Windows doesn't support the Teams COM add-in, also known as Teams add-in for Outlook. The new Outlook contains a native Teams meeting capability that enables users to schedule meetings. If you don't see the Teams meeting capability in new Outlook, see Teams meeting add-in missing in new Outlook for information on how to fix the issue.

## Symptoms

If you're a Microsoft Teams administrator, and your users can't install the Teams Meeting add-in for classic Outlook, schedule Outlook meetings from Teams, or schedule Teams meetings from Outlook, the issue might be caused by a problematic installation of the Teams Meeting add-in, a switch from classic Teams to new Teams, or because the users' mailboxes are hidden from the Global Address List (GAL). [...] ### Teams Meeting add-in is missing or its installation fails

If you configured the add-in for all users but it's missing for some users, try the following steps to troubleshoot and resolve the issue.

#### Check the status of the add-in in Outlook

Make sure that the Teams Meeting add-in is enabled in Outlook.

Microsoft Teams Meeting Add-in for Microsoft Office appears in Active Application Add-ins after Outlook restarts.

#### Reregister the Teams Addin Loader

Use the following steps:

Verify that users have the Teams desktop client installed. The meeting add-in can't be installed if you use only the Teams web client.

Verify that users are running Outlook 2016 or a later version.

Verify that all available updates for the Outlook desktop client are applied.

Exit Outlook. [...] Either you or your organization uninstalls classic Teams and then upgrades to new Teams. You uninstall the program by using one of the following methods:

After the upgrade, the Teams meeting add-in doesn't load and the add-in is removed from Outlook.

To reinstall the Teams meeting add-in in non-VDI environments, follow these steps:

Quit Teams.

Close the Outlook app.

Check the version of the Teams meeting add-in.

To check the Teams meeting add-in version, select Start > Settings > Apps > Installed apps, and then enter Teams Meeting Add-in in the search box.

results.title: Problem with calendar and Teams meeting invitations. - Microsoft Q&A
results.content:
For a personal Outlook.com account, try creating the meeting directly from Microsoft Teams Free.

Outlook Teams add-in does not support creating meetings with a personal account. Scheduling Teams meetings in Outlook is only available for Microsoft 365 Business Exchange accounts, and free Exchange accounts such as Outlook.com, MSN.com, and Hotmail.com are not supported for that Outlook add-in scenario. See Schedule a Microsoft Teams meeting from Outlook | Microsoft Support

To work around this:

- Go to Microsoft Teams Free and sign in with the same Microsoft account.
- Open Calendar.
- Create the meeting from Teams.
- Add the attendees, or use Copy meeting link / Share meeting invite.
- Send the meeting link in a normal Outlook.com email. [...] 1) Test a plain Outlook.com calendar invite without Teams

First, test whether a normal Outlook.com calendar invitation works without adding a Teams meeting.

- Sign in to Outlook.com Calendar.
- Create a new event from the primary Outlook.com calendar.
- Add only one attendee, preferably another Outlook.com account you own.
- Do not turn on Teams meeting or online meeting.
- Select Send.
- Ask the recipient to check:
  
  - Inbox
  - Junk Email
  - Deleted Items
  - Other
  - Search results for the event title

This helps confirm whether the problem is with calendar invitation delivery in general or only with Teams meeting invitations.

2) Send Teams meetings from Microsoft Teams Free instead of Outlook [...] To contact support:

- Sign in to Outlook.com Mail.
- Select Help on the menu bar.
- Search for calendar invitations not delivered.
- If the self-help options do not resolve the issue, scroll to Still need help? and select Yes.
- Include these details in the support request

results.title: Why the Teams Meeting link on Outlook is showing long URL instead of Join the Meeting now - Microsoft Q&A
results.content:
I’ve taken the time to review this behavior and test it on my side as well. While Outlook (classic) now inserts the full Teams meeting URL by default, there is still a reliable way to restore the familiar and user-friendly “Join the meeting now” link through manual formatting.

Please follow the steps below as a workaround:

1. In the meeting invitation body, highlight the full Teams meeting URL and cut it (Ctrl + X). User's image
2. Type Join the meeting now where you would like the link to appear.
3. Highlight the text “Join the meeting now,” then right-click and select Link. User's image
4. In the Address field, paste the meeting link you cut earlier, then click OK. User's image [...] This will embed the meeting URL behind the text, resulting in a clean, clickable “Join the meeting now” link that you can also format or highlight in color as needed.

I completely understand that this requires extra steps compared to the previous experience, and I appreciate your patience while Microsoft continues to evolve the Outlook and Teams integration. Please know that your feedback is valid, and scenarios like yours help highlight why consistent formatting is important.

I recommend submitting feedback directly to Microsoft via the Feedback Portal to help prioritize this feature in future updates.

Sharing your experience through this channel is the most impactful way to advocate for a change that would benefit you and other users. [...] 1. Check for Updates: Ensure that your Outlook is updated to the latest version, as updates can sometimes change how features work.
   2. Link Shortening Settings: If your organization has specific policies regarding link shortening, you may want to check with your IT department to see if there are any settings that can be adjusted.
   3. Use the Full URL Option: If you prefer using the full URL, you can right-click the link and select Show Full URL to access the complete link without it being shortened.

   If these steps do not resolve the issue, consider reaching out to Microsoft Support for further assistance specific to your version of Outlook.
